title: Guitar TAB Basics: Six-String Layout, Frets, Chords, and Rhythm Essentials
summary: JustinGuitar’s beginner-focused tutorial introduces guitar tablature (TAB) as a practical alternative to traditional notation for guitarists. The video explains that TAB uses six horizontal lines representing the six strings, with the bottom line corresponding to the thickest (low E) string and the top line to the thinnest (high E). Numbers on the lines indicate frets to press, while a zero means the string is played open. The presenter demonstrates a C-like idea of fretting across the six strings by showing an E major-like layout (0-2-2-1-0-0) and explains that notes can be played on multiple strings, so rhythm in TAB is not shown by default. He also notes that fingering isn’t specified by TAB—the learner must apply logic or follow guidance—emphasizing that early TAB literacy is a valuable skill. The video concludes by contrasting TAB’s lack of rhythm notation with the importance of listening to a riff or song for rhythm and by recommending that beginners begin reading TAB as soon as possible.
